chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The bringer (of the food) is Graced with sustenance, and the monopoliser is an accursed'.

key_terms.الْجَالِبُ: The bringer; one who brings goods to the market for sale.
key_terms.الْمُحْتَكِرُ: The monopoliser; one who hoards goods to raise prices.
key_terms.مَرْزُوقٌ: Graced with sustenance; provided for by God.

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on hoarding and monopolizing goods in the market?
ai.summary: This concise hadith from al-Kafi encapsulates the Shia jurisprudential stance on market ethics, distinguishing between the productive merchant who circulates goods (al-Jalib) and the speculator who artificially restricts supply (al-Muhtakir). It reflects the Imams' emphasis on preventing economic injustice and ensuring fair access to necessities, a principle deeply rooted in the concept of 'Ghabn Fahish' (excessive exploitation) in Shia commercial law.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ja’far Bin Muhammad Al Ashary, from Ibn Al Qadah, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The bringer (of the food) is Graced with sustenance, and the monpoliser is an accursed’.
en.sarwar: 6. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Ash’ariy from ibn al-Qaddah who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Messenger of Allah has said,
’One who supplies the market receives his sustenance and a hoarder is condemned.’”
